territorial_scope.description: Designates the Google undertaking, including non-UK parent and subsidiary entities, in a digital activity linked to the UK.

evidence.quote: we are designating Google as having SMS in the provision of its Mobile Platform with effect from the date of this Decision.

summary.short: The CMA's decision designates Google as having strategic market status (SMS) in the provision of its Mobile Platform (Android operating system, Play Store and Chrome/Blink browser engine) under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, effective from 22 October 2025 for five years. It imposes no conduct requirements.
summary.long: This CMA decision designates Google as having strategic market status (SMS) in the provision of its Mobile Platform under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 (the Act). The CMA finds that the Google undertaking (Alphabet Inc., Google LLC, Google Ireland Limited and Google UK Limited) meets the turnover condition, has substantial and entrenched market power, and holds a position of strategic significance. The Mobile Platform is one grouped digital activity comprising the Mobile Operating System (Android), Native App Distribution (Google Play Store) and the Mobile Browser and Browser Engine (Chrome and Blink), linked to the UK. Mobile devices themselves, third-party native apps and sideloading are outside the defined activities. The designation takes effect on the date of the decision and lasts five years, subject to review or revocation. The Act imposes no automatic rules; any conduct requirements or pro-competition interventions require further public consultation. The decision makes no finding of wrongdoing.

notes: Part 1 of 4 covers the summary, regulatory context, undertaking and turnover, and the digital activity definitions with the UK link. Relation target IDs and entity LEI/ticker fields are blank because the input gives no registry IDs and the document gives no verified identifiers. Some figures are redacted or given as ranges in this published version. The text states the designation finds no wrongdoing (1.3) and that the Act imposes no automatic rules on designated firms (2.29). In section_status, the entries above are present; the 'not_applicable' status is set only because the schema requires one, not as a finding that no such provisions exist. Part 2 of 4 (para 5.17 to para 6.136, with footnotes). It records no enabling power, amendment, repeal or implementation relation; the decision's legal basis is not stated in this part, and the Act appears only as 'the Act' and 'DMCCA'. Shares, price bands and commission rates are reported as published, in ranges and with [✄] redactions of confidential material; no redacted figures are coded. Internal inconsistency: para 6.18 describes Google's share as stable in each of the last eight years, while para 6.90(a) says stable over the past seven years. Chapter 6 conclusions on competitive constraint are the CMA's findings and are not coded here. Part 3 of 4 covers paragraphs 6.137 to 7.138 (barriers to entry, competition from alternative app stores, sideloading, web apps, cloud gaming, super apps, AI-based distribution, non-mobile alternatives, and the start of the browser chapter). No statutory basis, enabling power or legal instrument is named in this part, so no legal_basis relation is recorded; references to section 69 and section 174 notices appear without naming the statute. Figures in square brackets (e.g. '[✄] [0 – 1] million') are redacted or range-banded confidential values and are not coded. Internal note: para. 7.2 lists Amazon's Appstore as an example of an alternative app store, while footnote 695 states it is no longer supported on Android since August 2025. Many figures and findings report party submissions; the text states which submissions were given weight (e.g. para. 7.24, where access-to-functionality evidence was not relied on). Part 4 of 4 covers the end of Chapter 7 and all of Chapter 8 (profitability, forward-looking constraints, SMS and POSS conclusions). Only relations and entities are coded here; no events, thresholds, obligations or definitions. Target IDs, LEI and ticker are empty strings because the schema has no null option and no registry lookup was made. Many figures are redacted as [✄] with bracketed ranges; no exact values are coded. The Act is referred to only as 'the Act' in this part.
